# dsh-mac-use
**Computer-use for DeepSeek Harness on macOS.**

Let an agent _see_ the screen, _drive_ the mouse and keyboard, and _open_ apps and URLs —
the same o

bserve → act → verify loop as Claude's `computer` tool or Codex computer-use,
shipped as a single De
epSeek Harness bundle.
-lightgrey>)
## Why

Most computer-use setups ship a separate helper binary that needs its own screen-recording
and acces
sibility grants. `dsh-mac-use` doesn't:

- **Plugin only, no extra binary.** Everything runs inside the DeepSeek Harness Desktop
host process

. Screen capture uses the bundled `screencapture` tool; mouse/keyboard and
window inspection call ma

cOS APIs through the `koffi` FFI library (an npm dependency).
- **Permissions come from the Harness

app itself.** Because the plugin runs in the Desktop
host (a child of the Electron app), macOS check

s Screen Recording and Accessibility
against _DeepSeek Harness_. Grant those two once — never to a h

elper.
- **Virtual agent cursor.** Mouse actions don't strand your real pointer: clicks land,
then y

our cursor snaps back, while a blue arrow (white outline, ~2x size) glides between
action points wit
h its tip on the exact target — and it disappears when the task is done.

A system-prompt section teaches the agent the workflow: observe → locate → convert image
pixels to g
lobal points → act → screenshot again to verify.
## Accessibility snapshots

`computer_ax_snapshot` reads a macOS app's Accessibility (AX) element tree as compact
text instead o

f an image. One window costs a few hundred tokens — versus ~1,500 for a
screenshot — and works with

text-only models, which can read the hierarchy directly and
pick the `[ref]` to act on next.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **Cheap and text-only.** A snapshot is a few hundred tokens and readable by any model —
no vision

required.
- **Screen coordinates.** Each `@{x,y,w,h}` frame is in global display points, top-left
or

igin — the same space as `computer_move` / `computer_click`.
- **Refs.** The `[n]` index on each lin

e is stable for that snapshot; a later phase will
accept a ref to act on the element directly.
- **B

ounded.** It walks to `maxDepth` (default 8), visits up to `maxNodes` (default 300)
nodes, caps the

text at `maxChars` (default 12,000), and stops after ~1.5 s so an
unresponsive app can't freeze the

agent. When it stops early, `truncated` is `true` and
the text ends with a `… N more nodes not shown

the text ends with a `… N more nodes not shown` line.

## Requirements

- **DeepSeek Harness Desktop** (the macOS app), running on macOS (Apple Silicon).
- A **vision-capab

le model** for full observe-and-act (e.g. `deepseek-flash`, which reads
images). Text-only models ca

n still use `computer_ax_snapshot`, `computer_screen_info`,
and the action tools.
### Permissions (once)

1. **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording** → enable **DeepSeek Harness**.
2. **S

ystem Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility** → enable **DeepSeek Harness**
(needed for mous

e/keyboard input).
3. Fully quit and reopen DeepSeek Harness.
Missing a permission? The relevant tool fails with a message naming the exact setting.

e `plugin_manager` tool's `install_bundle` accepts the same targets.

The only dependency is `koffi@3.1.1` (the version the Desktop runtime ships). It bundles a
prebuilt

`darwin-arm64` binary and its install script is a fast prebuild check — no
compilation. pnpm 11 may

ask you to approve that script once: click **Allow these scripts

you to approve that script once: click **Allow these scripts

## Security

These tools drive the real desktop — treat them as powerful. They run under the agent's
normal permi

ssion/approval policy; keep them in a preset that prompts before acting, and
have the agent re-check

its work with a follow-up screenshot. macOS-only: on other
platforms the tools register but error w

ith a follow-up screenshot. macOS-only: on other
platforms the tools register but error when called.
